units: <cite ref="Taanit 26a:1">Taan. 26ᵃ</cite> top <he>על נפש … וכ׳ מלאה</he> when the appetite is satisfied and the stomach filled.
<cite ref="Shabbat 151b:4">Sabb. 151ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 12:6">Koh. XII, 6</cite>) <he>זה הכ׳</he> ‘the pitcher is broken’, that means the stomach.

<cite ref="Ecclesiastes 12:6">Ib.</cite> <he>לאחר שלשה … כְּרֵיסוֹ נבקעת וכ׳</he> three days after burial one’s stomach bursts open … saying (to the mouth), Take what thou hast put into me; Koh. R. to l. c.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:3:5">Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᶜ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 100">Gen. R. s. 100</cite>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 16a">Keth. 16ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כְּרֵיסָהּ בין שיניה</he> her belly extends to her teeth, i.e. she cannot deny her pregnancy.
Koh. R. to VII, 8 [read:] היה מפעפע בכְרֵיסָהּ כאריסה וכ׳ burned in her stomach like the venom of &c.; [Y. Snh. X, 28ᵈ top ככריסה, v. חֲכִינָה]; a. fr.—Esp. the stomach of ruminants, maw.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 3:1">Ḥull. III, 1</cite> <he>הכ׳ הפנימית</he> the inner stomach, expl.

<cite ref="Chullin 50b:5">ib. 50ᵇ</cite> <he>כל הכ׳ כולו … ואיזהו כ׳ החיצון וכ׳</he> (masc. !) the whole maw is called the inner stomach, and the outer stomach is the flesh (muscle) which covers the largest portion of the stomach; <cite ref="Chullin 50b:4">ib.</cite> (another opinion) <he>טפח בוושט סמון לכ׳ וכ׳</he>, corrected; <he>טפח בכ׳ סמוך לוושט</he> one handbreadth of the stomach where it joins the gullet is called the inner stomach; [oth. defin., v. <cite ref="A02572"><he>אִסְתּוֹמְכָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="D00462"><he>דִּיבָא</he></cite> a. <cite ref="M01196"><he>מֵילַת</he></cite>].—Pl. <he>כְּרֵיסוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Sukkah 21b:2">Succ. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>שכְּרֵיסוֹתֵיהֶן רחבות</he> whose bellies are broad (projecting further than the rider’s body; <cite ref="Tosefta Parah 3:2">Tosef. Par. III</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Parah 2:2">II</cite>), 2 <he>שכְּרֵיסָן רחבה</he>).
